newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish March retail sales value up 2.5 pct m/m - CSO.
newsitem.headline: Irish March retail sales value up 2.5 pct m/m - CSO.

text.p: The value of Irish retail sales rose a provisional seasonally adjusted 2.5 percent in March, giving a year-on-year increase of 7.0 percent, Central Statistics Office (CSO) data showed on Friday.

In February, the value of retail sales fell 0.7 percent over the month and was up 6.0 percent year-on-year. This was revised from provisional estimates of a 0.9 percent monthly fall and 5.8 percent annual rise.
The CSO said the value index was a provisional seasonally-adjusted 142.1 in March and a final 138.7 in February.
NOTE - Ireland's key inflation indicator is the Consumer Price Index (CPI) which was published on May 8, showing a month-on-month rise of 0.1 percent in April.
